text: Unlike Egret-6, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Plover-3 is $355k. Nobody should assume the budget of Plover-3 applies to Egret-6, the budget differs. An older draft of this note was archived.
The retirement date for Tern-3 is April 17, 2027; after that day it stops serving.
All instances of Tern-3 live in the datacenter at Tallinn. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
The retirement date for Plover-3 is April 12, 2027; after that day it stops serving. An older draft of this note was archived.
Questions about Teal-5 start with its owner, the Harbor team; they triage anything filed against it.
For Tern-3 the port is 5444. Changing the port needs a change ticket.
Source for Egret-6 is written in Go; no other language is allowed in its repository.
The primary datacenter of Pipit-9 is Lisbon; failover is handled by operations.
The owner of Curlew-4 is the Tessera team, and every change to Curlew-4 goes through their review.

Unlike Pipit-9, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Curlew-4 is Jolene Nakamura. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Curlew-4 applies to Pipit-9, the pager rotation differs. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
The yearly budget for Tern-3 is $3050k, covering licences and hosting.

Unlike Plover-3, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Teal-5 is the Nairobi datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Teal-5 applies to Plover-3, the datacenter differs. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
For Pipit-9 the port is 8955. Changing the port needs a change ticket.
Teal-5 listens on port 7770; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Finance fixed the budget of Curlew-4 at $2415k, reviewed every quarter. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The language of Tern-3 is Elixir, which new contributors must know.
The owner of Egret-6 is the Trellis team, and every change to Egret-6 goes through their review.

Unlike Curlew-4, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Plover-3 is the Osaka datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Plover-3 applies to Curlew-4, the datacenter differs.

Unlike Plover-3, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Pipit-9 is 2350 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Pipit-9 applies to Plover-3, the rate limit differs.
Avery Fairbanks is on the pager rotation of Egret-6 this month, with a deputy as backup.
The yearly budget for Egret-6 is $3200k, covering licences and hosting.
Plover-3 enforces a rate limit of 3250 requests per minute per caller. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
For Egret-6 the port is 5457. Changing the port needs a change ticket.
Plover-3 is implemented in Haskell; the language was chosen for its tooling. Details change slowly, so check the history first.

Unlike Tern-3, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Pipit-9 is Zig. Nobody should assume the language of Pipit-9 applies to Tern-3, the language differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.

Unlike Tern-3, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Teal-5 is May 13, 2029. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Teal-5 applies to Tern-3, the retirement date differs.
Unlike Pipit-9, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Curlew-4 is Erlang. Nobody should assume the language of Curlew-4 applies to Pipit-9, the language differs.

Unlike Tern-3, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Curlew-4 is the Dublin datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Curlew-4 applies to Tern-3, the datacenter differs. An older draft of this note was archived.

Unlike Egret-6, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Pipit-9 is Talia Valdivia. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Pipit-9 applies to Egret-6, the pager rotation differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The language of Teal-5 is Haskell, which new contributors must know.
